column1: # Which registry entry each bench panel scores, and where its sequences come from.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `scripts/bench_panel.py` takes one --panel, one --assay and
# one --fasta, so it cannot be looped over docs/bench-panels/*.tsv without knowing
# which assay each panel belongs to. Until 2026-10-26 that mapping lived only in
# shell history and in the table in docs/2026-10-21-M1-identity-aware-penalty.md,
# which is where every row below was read from and re-checked against the registry.
# `scripts/rescore.py` reads this to score every panel for a candidate strategy,
# which is Part 0.4's "bench panels: band/no-band accuracy per panel".
# A panel is a design paper's own test set, so it is the only truth below the assay
# level. `paper` is the independence unit: leave-one-panel-out means leaving out a
# whole paper, never a row, because the rows of one panel share a primer pair and a
# lab. The two Meyer files are ONE paper and must be left out together.
# `role`: fitting = a model may be fitted on it. control = specificity only, never a
# fitting set, because its negatives are other genera and teach "sequence far from
# the target gives no band", which scoring.max_pair_evalue already answers.
